paper_title: Incorporating Domain Knowledge into Materials Tokenization
caption: Comparison of Macro-F1 scores for MATTER and w/o material knowledge across during tokenization training different number of tokens.
model_annotation: The plot compares the Macro-F1 scores (%) of two tokenization methods—“MATTER (ours)” and “w/o material information”—as a function of the number of tokens, ranging from approximately 0.5 to 1.5 on a linear scale. The x-axis, labeled “Number of tokens,” displays values at regular intervals (0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4), while the y-axis, labeled “Macro-F1 Score (%)”, spans from 48 to 58 with major ticks every 2 units. The “MATTER (ours)” method is represented by a red line with circular markers and a light red shaded confidence region, showing a general upward trend from around 54.5% at 0.5 tokens to a peak of approximately 58% at 1.0 tokens, followed by a decline to about 50.5% at 1.5 tokens. The “w/o material information” method is shown with a purple line and circular markers, along with a light purple shaded confidence region; it starts at approximately 52% at 0.5 tokens, remains relatively flat around 52–53% until 1.4 tokens, and then drops sharply to about 48% at 1.5 tokens. The shaded regions indicate variability or confidence intervals for each method, with the red region consistently higher than the purple region across most of the token range, except near 1.5 tokens where both decline sharply.
